summary: This program defines a single growPlant method that takes sunlight and water as parameters, then prints a growth status based on those values. It shows how parameters let one function handle many different situations instead of hard-coding the values inside.

lines.text: The two values in the parentheses are the arguments: they are copied into the method's parameters in order, so sunlight becomes true and water becomes 3.

lines.code: public static void growPlant(boolean sunlight, int water) {
lines.text: The parameter list declares a type and a name for each incoming value, and inside the method body those names behave like ordinary local variables.
Joining text to a boolean with + converts the boolean into the words "true" or "false" automatically.
The conditional operator picks the first string when the test is true and the second when it is false, so both parameters must cooperate for the plant to be growing.
